findings.text: The opening paragraphs say plainly what Athena is, what a study is, and that this page is one study of firstmate. A newcomer can say what the page is within three short paragraphs.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository." (header lede)

findings.text: Why the page matters is given only from Athena's side, as a demonstration. It never says why a firstmate user or a curious newcomer should care about firstmate's states. Someone who arrives for Athena gets one sentence about it, then a long technical study of a different project.
findings.source: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim"

findings.text: The page ends with clear next steps: links for Athena and for firstmate, and a way to check any statement. The reader knows what to do next.
findings.source: Next steps: "Learn about Athena, and how to install and try it: https://github.com/doodla/athena"

findings.text: 'Captain' and 'yolo' are used in the first section with no definition there. They are defined only in a glossary far down the page, and the 'Start here' text does not link to it.
findings.source: What firstmate is: "With the yolo setting off, the captain approves every PR merge"

findings.text: 'Home' is never defined, including in the glossary, so a newcomer cannot tell what a secondmate or 'this home' means.
findings.source: What firstmate is: "A secondmate is a persistent home, not a backlog item."; claim c1: "refuses when this home has no item for the work"

findings.text: The design-choice cards have bare ids as titles, so a reader can only find out what each card is about by reading it all the way through.
findings.source: Why it is built this way: card headings "ra1" … "ra6"

findings.text: A merge that leaves the work in Ready, while t4 says a landed merge leads to Done, is confusing without more explanation. The same goes for 'reopened' being tagged "terminal-success" when the item is left open.
findings.source: t10 "ready → ready": "With yolo on, firstmate merges green, in-scope work itself"

findings.text: Small slips in the claims list (repeated source links and claims out of order) make the evidence section look less careful. They do not block understanding.
findings.source: Claims and sources: claim c2 lists "docs/configuration.md:357-357" twice; c14 and c42 also repeat a source; c34 appears before c33
